body.p: Arka's father was a Molkon. He found a small child. He raised it. Arka grew and became a great shaman. Arka competed with a shaman in shamanizing, he competed with the spirits. Who is stronger. They lit a big fire, dragged seven dead trees there. There they started to shamanize. They shamanized for one day, the shaman burned his spirits in the fire. The other shaman lost, he flew away, he burned his spirits. Arka's spirit grew in size. There were thirty swordsmen. When he lit the fire, they themselves said to the shaman: "It shall be so." That shaman flew away. Arka went to the other shamans again; the other shaman scolded Arka again; he said: "Why are you doing this? Lighting the Evenki on fire?" Arka said: "How am I lighting them on fire? He called me himself." Again the shaman said: "Let us shamanize, how he is a strong man." Arka said: "You yourself call. If you like, let us shamanize." Again they lit a big fire, lit seven dead trees. It became a very big fire. One of them grew horns, Arka grew horns. They wrestled each other, they measured their strength, who is stronger. Arka won, [that one] disappeared. His spirits grew stronger, greater. The loser had fifty swordsmen. When they lost, the swordmen said: "If you would start, [it would be] worse." Arka met the third shaman [from the house of] Putugin. Arka started to fight on the ice of the river, he shot Arka in the forehead with a Yakut gun. Arka wiped his forehead, there is no blood, there is no wound. Arka's fifty swordsmen fought the shaman's fifty swordsmen on the ice. [The one from] Putugin lost. Arka's house was that of Tanimo. Arka killed everyone of Putugin. Arka lived at the Yeloguj. Putugin came from this [right] side.
